details: Bitcoin (BTC) saw a rebound, climbing towards $82,000 after a period of correction. This recovery was spurred by U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement ruling out immediate military action against Iran, which helped alleviate geopolitical uncertainties and contributed to a dip in oil prices. Adding to the positive sentiment, market expectations for an October interest rate hike have decreased. Despite these bullish factors, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs continued to experience significant outflows, and the broader crypto market recorded over $1 billion in liquidations.
title: Bitcoin Recovers to $82K Amid Easing Geopolitical Tensions, Rate Hike Bets Dim

details: U.S. spot Ethereum (ETH) Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have experienced substantial net outflows, totaling nearly $500 million over the five trading sessions concluding on October 9th. This marks a concerning nine-day streak of continuous withdrawals, with BlackRock's iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) accounting for a significant portion. Concurrently, derivative traders are increasingly taking on short positions for ETH, signaling a growing bearish sentiment within the market.
title: Wall Street Pulls $500M from Ethereum ETFs as Traders Load Shorts

details: Hardware wallet provider Ledger has launched an investigation into multiple customer reports of cryptocurrency losses. These incidents are linked to devices purchased from CryptoBilis, a third-party reseller based in Southeast Asia. Ledger has advised customers who acquired devices within the last 90 days to avoid initialization or, if already set up, to consider transferring their assets to new devices as a precautionary measure. Unconfirmed reports suggest potential losses exceeding $86 million.
title: Ledger Investigates Stolen Funds Reports From Southeast Asian Reseller

details: Alex Mashinsky, the former CEO of the now-bankrupt crypto lending platform Celsius, has reached a settlement with the New York Attorney General. The agreement includes a permanent ban from participating in the securities, commodities, and cryptocurrency industries. Additionally, Mashinsky faces a conditional payment obligation of up to $35 million to New York, which is contingent upon his compliance with terms from a federal plea agreement and serving his court-mandated prison sentence.
title: Former Celsius CEO Alex Mashinsky Receives Lifetime Crypto Ban in NY Settlement

details: Greece has introduced a draft legislative proposal that would impose a 10% capital gains tax on profits generated from cryptocurrency transactions. This marks the country's first comprehensive framework for crypto taxation. The proposed law also includes an annual exemption for gains up to €500. The bill is currently open for public consultation, with a parliamentary vote expected to take place in November.
title: Greece Proposes 10% Capital Gains Tax on Cryptocurrencies, with €500 Exemption
